column1: # Which address-library ids each shipped pre-AE runtime cannot resolve.
# The client resolves every game address through an AE-era address library id.
# On a 1.5.x runtime it instead loads a translation table,
# GameFiles/Skyrim/SKSE/Plugins/versionlib-ae-to-se-<version>.map, because the
# pre-AE libraries use a different id namespace (VersionDb::Load). An id that
# table does not carry does not fail loudly: VersionDbPtr asks for the
# zero-returning stub on legacy runtimes, so every call through it returns 0
# instead of running, and the client warns once
# ("address library id N is not mapped on game N.N.N.N").
# Ten of those maps ship, one per pre-AE build, and until now only the 1.5.97
# one was accounted for: Tools/missing_1_5_97_ids.txt declares its gap and
# Tools/Scripts/check_docs.py compares the declaration against the map. Nothing
# looked at the other nine, which is how id 16113 came to be missing from
# three of them while the other seven carry it. This file is that record, and
# Tools/Scripts/check_map_coverage.py is what holds it to the maps.
# Columns: runtime <TAB> ae_id <TAB> why. '* <TAB> ae_id' means every shipped
# pre-AE runtime. Every shipped map's gap must be exactly the set declared for
# it, and every id declared here must really be absent from it - so this file
# cannot rot into claiming an id is missing after it has been recovered.
# The cost of the '*' rows, one by one, is in Tools/missing_1_5_97_ids.txt; that
# file stays the 1.5.97 declaration and the two are cross-checked rather than
# trusted to follow each other.

column1: # The three rows below are the 1.5.3/1.5.16/1.5.23-only gap, and it is not an
# oversight - it is not closable from anything in this repository. A map is a
# translation through the pre-AE namespace: an AE id names a pre-AE id, and each
# library spells that id as its own RVA. The other seven maps prove the rule -
# they all carry 16113, and every one of those values is exactly
# 0x1e7570 from 1.5.73 on). Those three libraries have no id 15873 at all: the
# pre-AE id space evolved rather than grew, so 1.5.3 names 791088 ids - 15376 of
# them unknown to 1.5.97 - while not naming 2962 that 1.5.97 does, 15873 among
# them. There is therefore no value to translate to and no override that could
# supply one: a value must be measured per build, and 0x1e7570 is not even an
# offset the 1.5.3 library lists. Regenerating cannot help either; VersionDb
# falls through to the zero-returning stub instead.
# It is live: ExtraContainerChanges::Data::GetArmor resolves it, and
# Actor::IsWearingBodyPiece() reads it. Unmapped, GetArmor can only answer
# "nullptr", which that predicate reads as "not wearing a body piece", and
# InventoryService::RunNakedNPCBugChecks re-dresses the actor on that answer.
# The call site was changed to require a definite answer instead, so those three
# runtimes degrade to "no repair" rather than "repairs the wrong way"; restoring
# the repair needs the three RVAs measured off the executables, which nothing
# here can do - see docs/FOLLOW-UP.md section 5. check_map_coverage.py's
# agreement rule is what keeps the other seven honest in the meantime.
